Lead times are significant—often 18 weeks or more—creating potential schedule risks for transformer assembly.4 Bushings: High-voltage bushings are another supply chain concern. Hitachi Energy manufactures bushings domestically, but production is generally limited to the ≤235 kV class. For higher ratings, utilities must rely on imports, which face longer lead times compared to OLTCs.5 Synthetic esters: Several companies produce and supply synthetic and natural esters used for transformers in the United States (Table 2). Compared to traditional mineral oils, ester dielectric fluids are more biodegradable and less flammable. Table 2. Cargill started producing ester fluid in the United States after purchasing Cooper Industries in 2012. Their fluid Envirotemp 360 (a synthetic ester) and FR3 (natural ester from soybean oil) are widely used (Cargill 2012). Cargill plans to further diversify its product line in 2025 by launching a new synthetic ester fluid called “SE3” (Cargill n.d.). MIDEL 7131 is another ester fluid produced by Shell lubricants with operations in Atlanta, Georgia (M&I Materials 2016). Ergon, a Mississippi-based specialty oil refiner, added synthetic and natural ester fluids to its portfolio in June 2022 (branded HyVolt SE for synthetic ester and HyVolt NE for natural soy- based ester) (Ergon 2022). Although accurate production levels are propriety and confidential, the existence of multiple manufacturing sites and no major market factors indicating the shortage of ester fluids signals a robust capacity to meet the domestic consumer demand. We may conclude that there is flexibility in the supply chain of ester fluids, as it can be stockpiled and transported easily, unlike other LPT components. Chemically refined inputs are mostly used to make synthetic esters. There is limited domestic production of pentaerythritol (Penta), a common polyol for high-performance synthetic esters (such as pentaerythritol tetra fatty acid ester). Perstorp Polyols’ Toledo plant is the only U.S. plant producing Trimethylolpropane and Penta (Perstorp n.d.), and any interruption might create a bottleneck in the industry. 1.4 Manufacturing Stages and Upstream Inputs The manufacturing of LPTs for hydropower facilities is a multistage process involving precise engineering design and customization, specialized materials, and skilled labor. Certain stages from manufacturing to installation, detailed in Table 3, depend on critical raw material inputs that have their own supply chain vulnerabilities, making the process particularly sensitive to disruptions.
